newsitem.title: INDIA: W.Africa, Mediterranean, new oil sources for India.
newsitem.headline: W.Africa, Mediterranean, new oil sources for India.

text.p: Mediterranean and West African nations could emerge as alternatives to Middle East oil suppliers if India boosts its infrastructure and refining capacities, industry officials said on Wednesday.

"The growth rate in India is surely significant enough to interest producers of crude from other regions such as the Mediterranean and West Africa in this market," Adel Khalil Almoayyed, General manager of Baharain National Oil Company told an energy conference in the Indian capital.
India's annual demand for petroleum products is growing at about eight percent annually, energy experts at the conference said.

Almoayyed said opportunities for Mediterranean and West African nations existed because crude oil demand in their traditional markets of Europe and North America was growing at only about one to 1.5 percent.
"Rising (Indian) imports will create an opportunity for the distant crude producers to compete with the Middle East crude producers," he said.
But he said India must boost infrastructure needed to import oil in large quantities from Mediteranean and West Africa.
India consumes about 80 million tonnes of petroleum products annually, more than half of which is imported, mainly from the Middle East.
Almoayyed said demand for petroleum products was growing quickly, driven by rapid growth in India's transport sector, which accounts for about 42 percent of total petroleum product consumption.
"Additionally, substantial growth in naptha and fuel oil demand is perceived due to rapid expansion of petroleum and electricity projects," he said.
He added that demand for gasoline, now at very low levels, would quadruple by 2000.

Almoayyed said India's refining capacity was inadequate by world standards. "The existing facilities are inadequate to produce the large demand for middle distillates which amounts to approximately 60 percent of the total product demand."
Industry offficials expect India's refining capacity to increase to about 130 million tonnes a year by 2002 from 61.55 million tonnes now.
Almoayyed said India imported about 450 million barrels of crude per day and the government was planning to raise output by another 300 million barrels per day by end of the decade.
"Even with this optimistic scenario, crude oil imports will have to be over 400 million barrels per day by 2000," he said.
